key_insight: The paper shows that adding approximate inverse process models to model-based RL lets modular production systems learn directly in task space, improving control efficiency and training speed.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for flexible manufacturing because it can simplify distributed optimization and self-learning control across heterogeneous modules without explicitly modeling all actuation details.
method: Build lightweight feedforward approximate inverse models for each module.
Embed inverse models into the policy network of standard RL algorithms.
Train RL in task space to decouple actuation dynamics from state-space dynamics.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on a laboratory modular production testbed with heterogeneous modules and showed improved performance and faster training, especially for off-policy methods.
watch_item: The added inverse models may depend on the quality of approximation and could be sensitive when transferred to more complex or changing production setups.
paper_title: Distributed Optimization of Modular Production Systems using Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Inverse Models
